passage: Afreen arrived at the club forty minutes early, as always, to watch Coach Jagdish set up cones. Everything he said she wrote in a small notebook: keep your knees soft, look up, move before the ball does. Her footwork got better every week and she glowed when he said her name. Then one Thursday, in the heat, he made a girl who had missed a pass run laps without water and told the team, "Don't mention today's drill at home. Parents don't understand training." Afreen felt a strange cold in her stomach. She wanted his approval more than anything, and she still believed most of what he taught her. But she thought, that isn't right. That evening she told her father exactly what had happened.

qa.q: Where did Afreen write down what Coach Jagdish said?
Why did Afreen feel a strange cold in her stomach on Thursday?
qa.a: Because the coach made a girl run laps without water and told the team not to mention it at home. She still wanted his approval but sensed it was wrong.

qa.q: What would you advise Afreen to do about her coach?
qa.a: Keep learning the footwork and other useful skills but trust her own judgement, and tell a trusted adult like her father or a club official about anything that feels like mistreatment.

qa.q: How might the girl who ran the laps feel about Afreen telling her father?
qa.a: Perhaps relieved that someone spoke up, or worried about trouble. Either way, she was mistreated and told to stay silent, so being backed up could matter to her.

grounding: A player who worships her coach still learns from him but notices a line crossed and does not stay silent.

passage:
Vinita had trained with Vikas sir at the Nagpur badminton academy for two years. His word was law. If he said jump, she jumped higher. A nod from him lit up her whole week.
Before the state trials, she twisted her ankle in practice. It swelled up fast.
"Tape it and play," Vikas sir said. "And don't tell your parents. They'll make a fuss and you'll lose your chance."
Vinita nodded automatically. Then, on the bus home, it bothered her. Why keep it secret? The ankle throbbed.
She thought: he's a brilliant coach. And this was wrong.
At home, she showed her mother the ankle and told her exactly what sir had said. Her mother's face tightened. "You were right to tell me. No coach should ask you to hide an injury." She took Vinita to the doctor that evening and phoned the academy director before dinner.

qa.q: What did Vinita twist in practice?
How did Vinita feel on the bus home?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and conflicted, torn between her admiration for Vikas sir and the sense that hiding the injury was wrong.

qa.q: Which choice protected Vinita, and why did it matter?
qa.a: She used her own judgement and told her mother, which got her ankle checked and brought in the academy director.

qa.q: How does Vinita's mother see Vikas sir's instruction?
qa.a: She sees it as a coach crossing a line by asking a child to hide an injury, and acts the same evening.

grounding: A teen who follows her coach's every word notices when he crosses a line and tells a parent instead of staying silent.

passage:
"Yamini, I've filled in your tournament form. Just sign here."
"Sir, it says I'm fifteen. I'm sixteen. The under-16 cutoff…"
"Nobody checks. You're my best player. We need you in that team."
"But sir…"
"Don't you trust me?"
Yamini did trust Chaitanya sir. He'd changed her serve, her footwork, her whole game. When he praised her, she felt ten feet tall.
"I trust you with coaching, sir. But I won't sign something that isn't true."
"You'll let the team down?"
"I'd rather play in the right group."
Sir went quiet and walked away. Her hands shook.
At home she told her father everything. He read the form and said, "You did the right thing. He's a good coach, but this was wrong." He called the school sports head that evening. The next day Yamini's form was corrected, and she was entered in the under-18 group instead.

qa.q: What age did the form say Yamini was?
How did Yamini feel when Chaitanya sir asked her to sign?
qa.a: She felt torn and anxious, trusting him deeply but uncomfortable signing something false.
Yamini refused to sign and told her father, who reported it to the sports head, so her judgement protected her and the team.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya sir see Yamini's refusal?
qa.a: He seems annoyed and disappointed, since he wanted his best player in the team, and he walks away.

grounding: A teen who admires her coach keeps her own judgement when he crosses a line, refuses to lie and tells her father.
